subject: for reference: radioButtons with TRUE/FALSE as.logical workaround

messages.author: b949e0841d7e094b
messages.subject: for reference: radioButtons with TRUE/FALSE as.logical workaround
parts:
In ui.R, I had a checkboxInput:

    checkboxInput('header', 'Header', TRUE)

In server.R, I had:

    df <- read.csv(input$dataset$datapath, 'header'=input$header, 'sep'=input$sep, 'quote'=input$quote)

Then I changed the checkboxInput to a radioButtons:

    radioButtons(
      'header'
      , 'Header:'
      , 'choices' = c('Yes' = TRUE, 'No' = FALSE)
      , 'selected' = 'Yes'
    )

and it wasn't working anymore.

A bit of testing showed that input$header was returning "TRUE" as opposed to just TRUE, i.e. radioButtons wraps TRUE with double quotes.

So here is the workaround I used: wrap input$header with as.logical

    df <- read.csv(input$dataset$datapath, 'header'=as.logical(input$header), 'sep'=input$sep, 'quote'=input$quote)

Feel free to chime in if there was a better, more elegant way.

Is the difference in behaviour intentional? Why aren't radioButtons called radiobuttonsInput and/or checkboxInput called checkBox, for consistency, or is the difference in naming convention reflecting the difference in behaviour with the logicals?

messages.subject: Re: for reference: radioButtons with TRUE/FALSE as.logical workaround
parts: For checked-boxes there are only two possible outcomes so it's natural to return boolean values TRUE and FALSE. For RadioButtons there can be more than 2 possible values so it's more natural to represent them using strings, hence "TRUE" and "FALSE".
